summary: One blocker: the implementation does not handle tabs or newlines, and does not fully collapse 3+ consecutive spaces. The test written for this iteration does not cover those cases and therefore passed anyway.

findings.evidence:
normalize_whitespace('  a		b

c   d  ') returned 'a		b

c  d', expected 'a b c d'. str.replace("  ", " ") only matches a literal two-space substring once per occurrence — it does not touch 	 or 
, and doesn't fully collapse runs of 3+ spaces.
findings.description: normalize_whitespace does not meet two of the three acceptance criteria: it doesn't collapse tabs/newlines, and doesn't fully collapse long space runs.
findings.required_action: Replace the str.replace-based approach with something that treats any run of whitespace characters uniformly (e.g. a regex substitution), and add test cases that actually cover tabs, newlines, and 3+ consecutive spaces — not just a single double-space case.
required_validation: normalize_whitespace('  a\t\tb\n\nc   d  ') == 'a b c d'
A test asserting the above (or equivalent) exists and passes.

required_actions: Fix REV-001 before the next review pass.
